Plan by age: 45–65

The money decisions from 45 to 65, in the order they arrive

The twenty years before 65 hold most of the decisions that shape retirement: catch-up savings, when you can reach your own money, how to cover healthcare until Medicare, when to claim Social Security, and how to leave things in order.

Pick your age to see what usually happens at that stage, what to do now, the decisions and common mistakes, and the key 2026 numbers with links to the official source. Each event links to the WealthLanding tools and articles that help.

  1. 45–49Peak years, full plate
  2. 50–54The catch-up years
  3. 55–59Early-exit options
  4. 60–62Decision years
  5. 63–65Medicare countdown

The journey from 45 to 65

  1. 1
    Ages 45–49Peak years, full plate

    For many households the late 40s bring the highest income so far and the highest bills at the same time: teenagers heading to college, parents who need more help, and a mortgage that is not finished.

    Key birthdays: Any year

    • Your first real retirement readiness check
    • Kids' college costs
    • Caring for aging parents
    • Protecting your income and family
    Open ages 45–49 →
  2. 2
    Ages 50–54The catch-up years

    At 50 the tax code lets you save more each year, and for many households the end of child-raising costs frees up cash at the same time. These are often the most powerful saving years of a career.

    Key birthdays: 50

    • Catch-up contributions start at 50
    • Kids leaving home
    • Health costs jump
    • Divorce or widowhood in midlife
    Open ages 50–54 →
  3. 3
    Ages 55–59Early-exit options

    In the late 50s the rules on reaching your own money loosen: the rule of 55 for workplace plans, then 59½ for IRAs. That makes an earlier exit possible, sometimes by choice and sometimes because of a layoff or buyout.

    Key birthdays: 55 · 55 · 59½

    • Early access rules: 55 and 59½
    • Job loss, buyout or forced early retirement
    • Pension or lump sum choices
    • Downsizing or relocating, including abroad
    Open ages 55–59 →
  4. 4
    Ages 60–62Decision years

    This is when the big, hard-to-reverse decisions cluster: when to stop working, how to cover health insurance until Medicare, whether to convert pretax savings to Roth, and when to claim Social Security.

    Key birthdays: 60 · 60 · 62

    • The 60–63 super catch-up
    • Your retirement date and the Roth conversion window
    • Healthcare bridge before Medicare
    • Social Security: 62, full retirement age or 70
    • Spousal and survivor benefits
    Open ages 60–62 →
  5. 5
    Ages 63–65Medicare countdown

    Medicare at 65 is the last big deadline before retirement settles into a routine. Income from two years earlier sets your Medicare premiums, so the planning starts at 63. Missing the enrollment window can mean penalties that last as long as you have Medicare.

    Key birthdays: 63 · 65 · 65

    • IRMAA: income at 63 sets premiums at 65
    • Enrolling in Medicare at 65
    • Estate basics and beneficiaries
    • Final readiness check and a retirement paycheck
    Open ages 63–65 →
